1.say: Park both cars nose-to-nose close but not touching. Turn both ignitions off and leave them off.
placements: good/working car + dead/disabled car → parked nose-to-nose face-to-face with front bumpers close but not touching (in the video: maroon Lexus facing dark sedan in parking lot)
both ignition switches/keys → turned to OFF with engines off (in the video: red car's hood raised open over front engine bay with engine off)
watch_for: if the cables cannot reach both batteries, the fronts are parked too far apart
if you hear the engine or see dash lights, that car is still on - turn its key fully off
1.check_yourself: Both cars sit nose-to-nose close but not touching with both engines silent and the maroon car's red hood raised open over its front engine bay.
1.safety: Set both cars in Park with parking brakes on and engines off before you walk between them.

2.say: Lift both hoods and prop them open. Find the black box battery in each front engine bay.
placements: maroon/red car's sheet-metal hood → lifted up and propped open over front engine bay (in the video: held up open over V6 engine cover)
dark/black car's sheet-metal hood → lifted up and propped open over front engine bay (in the video: held open by wooden stick on right side with black battery exposed at front corner)
watch_for: if you grabbed the air-filter box or fuse box, it is not the battery - look for the black box with + and - posts and cables
if the hood wobbles, the prop is not secure - reseat it before you lean in
2.check_yourself: Both hoods are raised open and propped and a black rectangular battery is exposed in the front corner of each engine bay.
2.safety: Prop both hoods securely and keep fingers clear so a hood cannot slam shut.

3.say: Clip one red jaw-clamp to the dead battery's + terminal. Clip the other red jaw-clamp to the good battery's + terminal.
placements: first red jaw-clamp with red insulated handle → onto + / positive post of dead/bad battery, usually marked + or under red cover (in the video: left-front post on black battery in maroon car's right-front bay)
second red jaw-clamp with red insulated handle → onto + / positive post of good/working battery (in the video: + post on black DieHard battery in dark car's bay)
watch_for: if a red clamp is on the - / NEG post, polarity is wrong - move it to the + post
if red tips touch each other or the body, you will spark - keep them separated
3.check_yourself: Both red jaw-clamps grip only the + posts with copper teeth on metal and touch no other metal.
3.safety: Keep the two red clamp tips apart and off any metal until each is firmly on its + post.

4.say: Clip one black jaw-clamp to the good battery's minus terminal. Clip the other black jaw-clamp to bare unpainted metal ground on the dead car.
placements: first black jaw-clamp with black insulated handle → onto - / NEG post of good/working battery (in the video: - post on black battery in dark car's bay)

second black jaw-clamp with black insulated handle → onto unpainted bare-metal ground on dead/bad car away from battery (in the video: front crossmember bare metal just above left headlight on dark car)
watch_for: if the second black clamp is on the dead battery's minus post, move it to bare metal - the video shows ground, not the post
if the ground clamp sits on paint or plastic, it will not connect - wiggle it until teeth bite shiny metal
4.check_yourself: One black clamp grips the good battery's - post and the other black clamp grips bare unpainted metal on the dead car with all cables clear of fans.
4.safety: Keep the black clamp away from the dead battery's minus post; clip it to bare metal instead.

5.say: Turn the working car's key in its ignition switch to start it. Let it idle a few minutes to charge the dead battery.
placements: ignition key in working/good car → turned forward with hand in column ignition switch below dash to START then released to run (in the video: right hand turning key with dash lights lit and gauges sweeping)
watch_for: if the engine dies right away, you did not let it charge long enough - restart and wait longer
if a cable has fallen onto a belt or fan, stop and reroute it clear before revving
5.check_yourself: The working car's engine is idling with red-orange dash warning lights lit and all four clamps still firmly attached.
5.safety: Keep hands, clothes and cables clear of the spinning fan and belts while the engine runs.

6.say: Start the dead car with its key. Pull the clamps off ground-bad, black-good, red-good, red-bad and let the revived engine run.
placements: black jaw-clamp on dead-car bare-metal ground → lifted off ground point and held clear in air (in the video: removal order is ground-bad first)
black jaw-clamp on good battery - post → lifted off - terminal and held clear
red jaw-clamp on good battery + post → lifted off + terminal and held clear
red jaw-clamp on dead battery + post → lifted off + terminal last with all cables clear of bays (in the video: bays empty with no clamps on batteries)
watch_for: if you let two removed tips touch, you will spark - keep one clamp in each hand apart
if the revived car stalls, the battery is still low - reconnect in the same order and charge longer
6.check_yourself: Both engine bays have all jumper clamps removed from posts and ground and cables pulled clear of the batteries.
6.safety: Keep the removed clamp tips apart and off metal so they never touch each other.
